subject: Throughput sizing — post-call and SLO qualification
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Call recap — throughput & latency targets

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can move the sizing forward.

Summary of Finex workload:
- Primary product: real-time transaction enrichment (JSON responses) used in customer dashboards and alerting.
- Typical response payload: 250-400 tokens (mostly English + structured JSON fields).
- Traffic pattern: steady-state 300 QPS with 30 qps bursts up to 700 QPS for 10-15 minutes (end of day windows).
- Streaming: we use streaming for incremental UI updates; prefer chunked output as soon as tokens are available.

SLO targets:
- 95th percentile latency target: <= 300ms for first token; <= 700ms for complete response on baseline model.
- Concurrent sessions: ~1200 concurrent sessions during peak (clients hold connection while streaming).

Requested from Redwood: detailed throughput sizing (tokens/sec and required GPU pools), confirmation on streaming-first-token latencies with continuous batching, and any recommendations for quantization/batching to meet cost targets.

Attached a small sample of request traces and a CSV with QPS-per-minute for last 30 days (finex_workload_sample.csv).

Thanks — Alice
--
Alice Zhang
Head of Platform
Finex
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Call recap — throughput & latency targets

Thanks Alice — this is very helpful. Quick confirmation of next steps from our side and a couple of follow-ups:

Action items (Redwood):
- Rafael to produce a first-pass throughput/GPU sizing using your CSV and token assumptions.
- Marissa to validate streaming-first-token latency expectations with our runtime team.
- I will put together a short AMI that outlines tradeoffs (batching vs latency vs cost) and recommended configs.

Questions for Finex (to finalize sizing):
1) Can you confirm average tokens per request vs 95th percentile tokens per request? You mentioned 250-400 tokens — can you share the 95th percentile?
2) For the bursts, is the 700 QPS spike mostly read-only inference (no long chats) — i.e., are those single-shot calls or multi-turn streaming sessions?
3) Any hard SLA/penalty requirements for 95th p99 beyond the latency numbers you shared?

If you can drop the 95p token size and a short sample of payload types we can run a more precise sizing. Rafael — marking for you to start with the CSV Alice attached.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Zhang <alice@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Call recap — throughput & latency targets

Hi Neha — quick answers below and I attached our CSV slice and a short payload sample (same attachment set):

Answers:
1) 95th percentile tokens/request: 520 tokens. Average ~320 tokens.
2) Bursts are mostly single-shot inference for mass notifications; streaming sessions are a smaller portion (~15% of burst qps) but important for UI UX.
3) No formal SLA penalties for this phase; we’re trying to architect for 95p under 300ms first-token to avoid user-visible lag.

Attachment: finex_workload_sample.csv (5KB) — includes minute-level QPS for last 30 days and a small sample of request sizes.

Thanks — Alice
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@finex.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing — first pass

Hi Alice & Neha — I ran a first-pass calc using the CSV and the 95p token = 520. Key assumptions noted below. I also attached an XLS with the workbook (redwood_throughput_calc.xlsx).

Assumptions:
- Model choice: open-medium-1024 (approximate baseline for performance estimates).
- Average token cost path: continuous batching with prefix KV cache for repeated user context.
- Streaming: optimized runtime for first-token within an uncached path with small-batch priority.

Sizing results (ballpark):
- Steady-state 300 QPS, avg 320 tokens -> ~96k tokens/sec; 95p token 520 -> ~156k tokens/sec for heavy tail.
- Peak burst 700 QPS with 15% streaming = 700 * 520 * 0.85 (non-streaming tokens/sec) + streaming overhead: approximate peak tokens/sec ~364k tokens/sec.
- Concurrency estimate: 1200 concurrent sessions maps to ~1200 active KV entries; memory for KV cache sizing will be handled in separate pass.

GPU pool estimate:
- For steady-state (300 qps) we estimate 4 x A100-like GPUs with continuous batching and quantization to int8 could hit cost targets.
- For absorbing peak bursts without queuing beyond 200ms, recommend burst pool of 2 additional nodes that can spin up (or use Reserved Dedicated burst capacity).

Open items:
- Precise streaming-first-token latency: we need Marissa to run a controlled test on model variant to confirm 95p first-token numbers when continuous batching is enabled.
- KV cache warmup: need more workload traces showing repeated contexts to validate cache hit rates.

Happy to walk through the workbook — Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@finex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing — tests for streaming latency

Alice — quick note from runtime side. We can prioritize a small controlled test to validate first-token latency with continuous batching. Proposed test plan:
- Test config A: batching enabled (max batch 64), int8 quantized model variant, no KV cache warm (cold KV). Measure 95p first-token.
- Test config B: same as A but with KV cache warm for 60% of requests to simulate common user flows.
- Test config C: low-latency priority path (max batch 8) for streaming-first-token.

We expect config C to be the most relevant for meeting your 300ms first-token SLO for streaming flows; config A/B are cost-optimized for steady-state. Can you confirm which window to run the test against (we can reuse the CSV minute slice)? Also if you have a sandbox API key or can we spin up a short-lived test tenant?

Marissa
Runtime PM, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Zhang <alice@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing — tests for streaming latency

Thanks team — that plan looks good. We can provide a short-lived test tenant and a 1-hour production-like replay window from the CSV for the tests. Confirming:
- Use the minute-level spike window on 2027-02-28 17:45-18:15 PST for burst sim.
- Run config C first to validate first-token under 300ms for streaming; then run A/B for cost tradeoffs.

Please send over the test tenant details and any payload signing keys we need to add; I’ll open a ticket with our infra to allow Redwood IPs. HubSpot link: https://hubspot.com/deal/FINEX-224.

Alice
